CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who injured his right elbow approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He reports that his 13-year-old son was checking him multiple times with a lacrosse stick and may have struck him in the elbow area. He denies falling. The pain is sharp in character and is located at the tip of the elbow. Pain occurs with any movement of the elbow and radiates down the forearm. Patient tried ibuprofen for a couple of days with some relief. He reports usually forgetting to take it.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. Lungs are clear bilaterally.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension.
Diabetes mellitus type 2.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily.
Metformin 500 mg daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays lacrosse recreationally with his children, ages 13 and 10. He follows a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake with his family.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure: 150/90 mmHg (elevated).
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted (known prior).
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Right elbow: Pain to palpation of the olecranon area of the posterior elbow. Mild pain with flexion and extension. Normal range of motion. Mild swelling and bruising noted.

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: Normal, no fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion secondary to blunt trauma from lacrosse stick. Mild swelling and inflammation present. Prescribe ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and swelling. Ice three times daily for 20 minutes at a time. Avoid playing lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow healing. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Patient compliant with low salt diet. Blood pressure elevation may be related to white coat syndrome. Diabetes mellitus type 2: Continue metformin 500 mg daily. Recent blood glucose readings 80-100 mg/dL. Order HbA1c to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment needed.
